thread:
olga: Quick sync — customer A is trialing Nova-2.1b (gguf) next week. Need a lightweight onboarding + quant smoke playbook to validate quality vs cost tradeoffs. Proposing a "dual-path" approach: Path A = int8 symmetric per-layer + outlier clamp; Path B = fp8 dynamic with per-op fallback. Both get the same sample-weighted eval suite. Who can own run + short writeup by Thu EOD?

sam: I can own the runs. Planning to run 3 probe sets: 1) conversational instrs (N=300), 2) API logs subset (N=500, weighted by freq), 3) long-context summarization (N=100).

jeremy: +1. For the int8 path we should enable per-layer scale calibration and record layerwise MSE, then mark layers with MSE>threshold for mixed-precision fallback.

olga: Exactly — let's call the threshold 1.2e-3 MSE for now (tunable). Also capture user-facing metrics: instr-qa pass rate, rougeL for summarization, and mean token PPL delta vs fp16 baseline.

ci-bot: Build started for branch "onboard/nova-2.1b/dualpath-smoke" — CI will produce artifact with calibration stats and quantized weights. ETA ~40m.

eva: Small suggestion: sample-weighting should upweight high-frequency API prompts by 5x so we prioritize the common cases. We should also run a short latency/throughput check with our serving config (batching=auto, max_batch_size=32).

sam: Commands I'll run (local harness):

```
# smoke run
python tools/smoke_eval.py \
  --model-path models/gguf/nova-2.1b.gguf \
  --quant-mode int8-symmetric,fp8-dynamic \
  --samples-file tests/smoke_samples_weighted.json \
  --metrics ppl,instr_qa,rougeL \
  --save-calib outputs/nova_dualpath_calib.json
```

sam: Expected quick pass criteria (for smoke):
- instr-qa pass rate >= 90% (vs fp16 baseline)
- mean PPL delta <= 0.7
- rougeL drop <= 3 pts for summarization
- latency 95p within 1.5x of fp16 when batching=auto

jeremy: We'll also collect per-op fallback counts (fp16/float32 fallbacks) and KV cache hit impact on latency. If fallback rate > 4% on hot ops, mark for model-level rework or hybrid precision.

olga: Good. Owners: sam = run experiments + collate draft report, jeremy = analyze layer/op fallbacks and propose fallback thresholds, eva = ensure sample weighting + serving smoke, kim = review and sanity-check evaluation harness. Deliverables: short doc + artifact link + recommended quant profile (gguf meta).

kim: I'll slot time Thu morning to review. Can someone ping me when runs are done? @sam @jeremy

sam: Will post artifacts here + a tiny summary table. Plan: int8 run first, then fp8; expect int8 to be cheaper but higher risk on long-context tasks.

ci-bot: Build succeeded. Artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/onboard/nova-2.1b/dualpath/173_artifact.tar.gz

sam: Uploaded initial results snapshot: s3://redwood-results/onboard/nova-2.1b/dualpath/quick_snapshot.json — summary: int8 instr-qa 89.4%, fp8 92.1%; PPL delta int8 +0.6, fp8 +0.25. Attaching detailed calib file next.

eva: Those numbers look promising. If we can reduce int8 instr-qa delta by 1% with selective layer FP fallback it might be a win (2.8x cost vs fp16). Can we try layer cutoff automatically where MSE>1.2e-3?

jeremy: I'll run a targeted mixed-precision pass tonight with layer fallback policy: `if layer_MSE>1.2e-3 => keep fp16 for that layer`. Will post results.

olga: Thanks all. After jeremy's mixed-precision pass we'll decide recommended default profile for Dedicated vs Hosted (hosted might default fp8 dynamic, dedicated customers can opt into tuned int8+fallback). Closing loop: sam will draft short runbook entries for console ops (how to pin profile, how to force fallback), kim to review docs, eva to sanity-check perf numbers. :thumbsup:

sam: noted, drafting runbook now — will link here when ready.
